tasks.title: Ingest the F-TRACT CCEP atlas
tasks.brief: Ingest F-TRACT, the only measured DIRECTED human connectivity dataset: Lemarechal J-D, Jedynak M, Trebaul L et al., 'A brain atlas of axonal and synaptic delays based on modelling of cortico-cortical evoked potentials', Brain 2022;145(5):1653-1667, PMID 35416942. 780 patients, 34,354 stimulations, 774,445 CCEPs, on HCP-MMP1 (360 parcels). EBRAINS DOI 10.25493/5AM4-J3F, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; the matrices are explicitly asymmetric. Direction here is measured causally in living humans: stimulation site to recording site IS a direction. Record the limitations at the source: electrode placement is clinically driven and biased toward temporal/frontal epileptogenic cortex, patients are not neurotypical, CCEPs can be polysynaptic so a directed edge is not necessarily monosynaptic, and the atlas is group-average only. DO NOT use TVB's connectivity_76/_96/_192 as a human alternative: they carry ordinal {0,1,2,3} weights and RM- prefixes and are macaque CoCoMac tracer codes mapped onto human coordinates, widely mis-cited as human DSI. NOTE 2026-08-25: read docs/ftract-recon.md before starting. The claim above that connectivity_76/_96/_192 all carry ordinal {0,1,2,3} weights and RM- prefixes was measured against the real files and holds only for connectivity_96; _76 and _192 carry 34 continuous values and l/r-prefixed CoCoMac labels. Test on several signatures, not that one.

tasks.title: Human PK parameters for the three drugs
tasks.brief: Replace the rat PK layer with human parameters. Route F: IV 1, transdermal 0.92, OTFC 0.50, buccal 0.65+/-0.20, sublingual 0.54, intranasal ~0.89, oral 0.31. fu ~0.156 (Meuldermans 1982, PMID 6214227). DIAZEPAM: Klotz 1975 PMID 1127104 open, n=33, t-half 20h at age 20 rising to ~90h at 80 with CL age-independent, 97.4% bound; Divoll 1983 PMID 6849499 F(oral)=0.94. TWO TRAPS: Scott & Stanski 1987 found NO age effect on fentanyl PK, since the dose reduction with age is purely pharmacodynamic, so no age-on-CL covariate may cite that paper; and the Lombardo 2018 curated fentanyl VDss = 0.89 L/kg is 4-6x below the label and every compartmental model, so it must not be imported blind.

tasks.title: Kp,uu with an explicit species-transfer factor
tasks.brief: This is the weakest layer in the pivot and the code must say so. Human has 6 compounds with paired measured Kp,uu,brain and Kp,uu,CSF against 70 in rat (Sato 2021, AAPS J 23(4):81, PMC8175309). Implement Kp,uu_human = Kp,uu_rat * f_species, with f_species ~1 for non-efflux substrates and ~2-3 for P-gp substrates, exposed as a FITTED parameter with those priors so the uncertainty is visible rather than buried in a constant. Justification for the direction: human P-gp does less work at the BBB than rat (fitted MDR1 relative activity 0.395 rat vs 0.096 human, Sato 2021), morphine Kp,uu 0.29 rat vs 0.64 human (Ederoth 2004, PMID 15025740, n=7 TBI patients, the only direct human opioid measurement), [11C]GR205171 brain:plasma ~9x higher in human than rat (Syvanen 2009, PMID 19047468). PER DRUG: diazepam uses the real human value Kp,uu,CSF = 0.79 (Friden 2009, PMID 19764786; the table is open in the DiVA thesis diva2:349401) and is not an efflux substrate so the CSF bias is small; haloperidol needs NO Kp,uu, since inverting the human occupancy curve gives the same quantity (see P16.1); fentanyl has no defensible human value, uses ~1, and must be flagged as the model's least-supported input. Record why the postmortem forensic route is refused, which drug_pk.py:2292 already argues correctly. Record the CSF surrogate's known bias: it OVERPREDICTS for highly effluxed drugs, and the human regression slope 0.34 is the worst of the three species.
acceptance: f_species is a fitted parameter with cited priors, not a hard-coded constant
Diazepam uses the measured human value; fentanyl is flagged least-supported
Haloperidol requires no Kp,uu and a test asserts it does not consume one
The CSF surrogate bias direction recorded where the value is consumed

tasks.title: Human PK validation
tasks.brief: Validate the human PK models against independent published curves, in the manner of P1.6. Record the structural hole honestly: there is NO adult diazepam population PK model: all four that exist are pediatric or methodological (Ku 2018 PMID 30267478, n=87 children). Everything adult is 1970s-90s intensive-sampling NCA, overwhelmingly from one group (Greenblatt/Shader, Tufts), and the pharmacogenetics is in a different unlinked population. Also record: no readable haloperidol two-compartment popPK (Pilla Reddy 2013, PMID 24113674, is paywalled and is the single most valuable missing parameter set), and no haloperidol depot popPK at all. Two documented rat-to-human failure modes worth encoding as tests: Johnson 2016 (PMID 26718955) swapped human popPK into a rat hybrid PBPK-PD and specifically UNDER-predicted human haloperidol D2 occupancy, attributed to unmodelled brain reduced-haloperidol back-oxidation and active BBB influx.

tasks.title: Occupancy-limited transducer (D2)
tasks.brief: D2 effect tracks fractional occupancy near-linearly in the 60-85% band, with Hill coefficient 1 in every published human fit. Build the occupancy-limited transducer and calibrate against human PET: Kapur 1997 PMID 9201802 (n=12, EC50 0.51 ng/mL, 80% at 2.0 ng/mL, r2 0.84); Fitzgerald 2000 PMID 10789875 (prospective, ED50 0.40 ng/mL, mean prediction error 3.89%); de Greef 2011 PMC3032087 (EC50 0.532 +/- 0.085, Emax 92.0 +/- 3.3, 12 studies/45 arms); Uchida 2011 PMID 21508857. Thresholds from Kapur 2000 PMID 10739409: response above 65%, hyperprolactinemia above 72%, EPS above 78% (NOT 80%). Dose-level validation target: Lako 2013 PMID 23948784, 51 studies, 606 patients, D2R(%) = OccMax * dose / (OccD50 + dose), haloperidol OccMax 91.9%, OccD50 0.65 mg/day; formulas openly reproduced in the CC-BY appendix of PMC10618092. This transducer is also what removes the need for a haloperidol Kp,uu, since inverting the curve yields unbound brain concentration.
acceptance: Occupancy transducer reproduces Kapur EC50 and the Lako dose-level curve

tasks.title: Reserve-dominated amplification (mu-opioid)
tasks.brief: An occupancy-to-effect map is the WRONG structure for mu-opioid: methadone at 18-90 mg/d shows no displacement and no dose-occupancy relationship at all (Melichar 2005, PMID 15347732). Port the open FDA receptor-to-ventilation model instead: github.com/FDA/Mechanistic-PK-PD-Model-to-Rescue-Opioid-Overdose (Mann J et al., Clin Pharmacol Ther 2022;112(5):1020-1032, PMID 35766413). Binding ODE dRL/dt = K_on*L^n*R - K_off*RL with R = 1 - RL; fentanyl K_on 3.081e-5, K_off 4.331e-3, n 0.8439, apparent K_D ~351 pM ~ 0.118 ng/mL; naloxone K_on 1.669e-4, K_off 3.959e-2, n 0.858. Drive reduced by CAR^P where CAR is fraction bound, with separate exponents for wakefulness drive and chemoreflex, estimated separately for naive and chronic users. Open subject-level raw data: Dryad 10.5061/dryad.j3tx95xdb (Moss 2022, PMID 35085249, 22 participants, the parent trial of Algera 2021). This also replaces the naloxone-rescue result v0 reproduced in rodent terms: Yassen 2007 PMID 17922561 (naloxone biophase t-half 6.5 min) and Olofsen 2010 PMID 20461002 (n=56).
acceptance: FDA binding constants ported and round-tripped against the published model

tasks.title: Operational model of agonism (GABA-A)
tasks.brief: GABA-A is reserve-dominated AND efficacy-dependent: lorazepam 0.03 mg/kg IV, a therapeutic dose producing marked sedation, occupies UNDER 3% of benzodiazepine sites (Sybirska 1993, PMID 8395663), so over 97% receptor reserve. Even zolpidem at twice its hypnotic dose reaches only 27 +/- 11% (Abadie 1996, PMID 8925872). Occupancy is nearly irrelevant to effect magnitude; intrinsic efficacy is what varies. Implement the operational model of agonism after Visser SA et al., J Pharmacol Exp Ther 2003;304(1):88-101, PMID 12490579: 9 GABA-A modulators, in-vivo affinity K_PD 0.41-436 ng/mL and in-vivo efficacy e_PD -0.27 to +0.54, with K_PD(unbound) versus in-vitro affinity r = 0.93 and e_PD versus in-vitro GABA-shift r = 0.95. Note that study is rat EEG, so it is a STRUCTURE to adopt, not values to import. The one human cross-species calibration point is TPA023: occupancy EC50 9 ng/mL human versus 19-30 rat/rhesus/baboon (Atack 2010, PMID 19779131). The only quantitative human benzodiazepine-site EC50s are for subtype-selective non-benzodiazepines (AZD7325 15 nmol/L, AZD6280 440 nmol/L; Jucaite 2017, PMC5263201).
acceptance: Affinity and efficacy separated as distinct fitted quantities

tasks.title: Rebuild the endpoint library on human readouts
tasks.brief: Replace the seven rodent endpoints with human physiological and pharmacological readouts in real units. OPIOID: isohypercapnic minute ventilation, fentanyl C50 0.42 +/- 0.07 ng/mL opioid-naive and 1.82 +/- 0.39 chronic (Algera 2021, PMC7983936, open); remifentanil miosis EC50 0.541 ng/mL, gamma 2.38, RSE 7% (Maharaj 2025, PMC11867082), the tightest parameter estimates in the opioid PD literature. BENZODIAZEPINE: midazolam BIS IC50 70 ng/mL gamma 8.6, MOAA/S IC50 80 ng/mL gamma 3.4 (Wiltshire 2012, PMID 22253270, n=81); EEG beta Mandema 1992 PMID 1611810 77 +/- 15 ng/mL; memory Cp50 midazolam 56 +/- 4 ng/mL (Veselis 1997, PMID 9357875), amnestic BELOW sedative concentration. ANTIPSYCHOTIC: prolactin, the closest existing analogue to what this project builds, with a full mechanistic popPK-PD (Petersson 2013, PMC3675734, 15,551 samples, N=1,000; tolerance is positive feedback, NOT precursor-pool depletion, which Friberg 2009 tested and rejected) plus dose-response in ng/mL (Lin 2025, PMC12423237, N=23,128, haloperidol peak +22.20 ng/mL at 8.5 mg/d). tasks.title: Effector-specific ke0
tasks.brief: ke0 depends on the effector, reproducibly across groups, and must not be shared across readouts: EEG 0.147 per min (t-half 4.7 min), respiratory t-half ke0 16.4-17.2 min, pupil t-half ke0 11.1-12.8 min. tasks.title: Retire the endpoints with no human analogue
tasks.brief: Retire into legacy/ the endpoints that have NO human analogue at all, and record why as a real result rather than a silent deletion. ANXIETY (elevated plus maze): the EPM is species-specific rodent thigmotaxis and open-space aversion; the nearest human analogue is subjective VAS anxiolysis, which de Visser 2003 (PMID 12534639) places among the LESS sensitive benzodiazepine biomarkers. tasks.brief: Validate the receptor-binding layer directly against human PET occupancy, which v1 structurally could not do. D2 is the strong case (Kapur 1997, Farde 1992 PMID 1352677, Nordstrom 1992). tasks.notes: Delivered: 15 human striatal D2 occupancy observations for haloperidol registered in src/neurocascade/human/pet_observations.py from 7 primary sources, each backed by a per-paper transcription fixture CSV under src/neurocascade/human/fixtures/ with a SHA-256 digest recorded in code and routed through HumanDatasetManifest; HumanDatasetManifest.checksum_proves states in words that a green checksum locks the transcription against drift and says nothing about fidelity to the paper. occupancy_observations() returns the eight points carrying a differenceable central occupancy value. HEADLINE NEGATIVE: no per-subject table of oral haloperidol dose against striatal D2 occupancy is reachable. The canonical series (Farde 1988 and 1992, Nordstrom 1992, Kapur 1996, 1997 and 2000) is paywalled exactly where the per-subject rows live, and pirate mirrors were excluded by instruction, so the three Kapur entries are registered as occupancy RANGES with observed_occupancy=None; a midpoint was available for the taking and was declined because no source prints one, and PETOccupancyObservation.contains() supports the only test such a point admits. (1) Videbaek is a 0.7 mg intravenous infusion reported on FREE plasma, so its route and its plasma basis both differ from the oral steady-state case the chain is being built for; of the eight differenceable points, four are on a free basis (Videbaek) and four are depot group means (Nyberg 1995, Regenthal 1997) whose abstracts name no tracer. (2) Region is None on 11 of the 15 points because the abstracts that carry them name no region. (3) Converting Videbaek's mean free Kd of 0.25 nM at the 9.0% free fraction recorded in P19.2 gives roughly 1.04 ng/ml total, against Kapur's 0.51 and Fitzgerald's 0.40 ng/ml: a 2 to 2.5-fold IBZM-versus-raclopride spread that sets the floor on how well any single-parameter chain can be expected to match the literature. tasks.brief: HumanReceptorParameter('D2') has ki_nM=None and efficacy=None with evidence_context 'in-vivo PET'. The quantity that actually predicts occupancy in vivo is a plasma EC50, not an in-vitro Ki; P15.4 named the in-vivo versus in-vitro correction but delivered only scaffolding. Fit or transcribe the human plasma EC50 for haloperidol D2 occupancy from the P19.3 observations, and separately record a human in-vitro D2 Ki together with its assay conditions. Report the measured ratio between the two rather than assuming they are equal, and state explicitly which one the occupancy model consumes.
acceptance: The D2 record is usable, with the in-vivo EC50 and the in-vitro Ki stored as separate cited fields

No in-vitro Ki is promoted into the occupancy path without the explicit correction applied
tasks.notes: Delivered: the D2 record is usable, and the two numbers that could have filled its single affinity slot are stored as separate cited fields. HumanReceptorParameter gained a ligand field (a Ki and an efficacy belong to a ligand at a receptor, not to the receptor), separate ec50_* and ki_* provenance fields, and an occupancy_constant_nM() that returns the in-vivo EC50 and refuses to hand back an in-vitro Ki unless the caller passes a correction factor AND names its source; usable now requires the in-vivo EC50, so a record holding only a Ki stays closed however well cited that Ki is, and a test constructs exactly such a record to prove it. IN-VIVO EC50, fitted not transcribed: 1.8849 nM total plasma (0.708 ng/mL), 95% profile-likelihood interval 1.382-2.525 nM, asymptotic SE 0.176, residual RMSE 0.036, from the four P19.3 observations carrying both a central occupancy and a total plasma concentration. Kapur 1997's and Fitzgerald 2000's published EC50s were available for one-line transcription and were DECLINED, because P19.6 validates the finished chain against Kapur's own occupancy ranges and transcribing his constant would have made that validation circular. Fitted by bisection on d(RSS)/d(EC50) rather than scipy curve_fit so the constant cannot move with a scipy version; a test asserts the recorded constant still equals the recompute and another asserts it is the least-squares optimum under perturbation. The two depot studies fit independently to 1.940 and 1.817 nM and bracket the pooled value, which is the replication that makes a four-point fit worth recording. Carried as caveats rather than smoothed: the four points are NOT independent (two studies x two timepoints on the same eight patients each), both published oral constants fall BELOW our interval and the IBZM-derived constant above it, and both source studies are depot IM steady state feeding an oral chain. Total and free plasma are never pooled (they differ ~11x here, which is protein binding, not biology); the one converted row is labelled converted. HEADLINE IN-VITRO RESULT: there is no single human D2 Ki for haloperidol. Seven primary measurements at cloned human D2 were retrieved in full text and they span 0.13 to 8.85 nM, a factor of 68, tracking tracer class and guanine-nucleotide state; sodium alone does not explain it, since the highest-sodium source (Sykes 2017, 138 mM) reports one of the lowest values and two [3H]spiperone sources never print their buffer at all. Every record carries a not_printed tuple so a blank condition field cannot be mistaken for a checked one. Binding and functional constants are kept apart: Kaczor 2023a reports Ki 6.56 nM against its own cAMP Kb of 0.11 nM, and 2023b 7.41 against 0.29, 20-60x apart inside single papers. The registry cites bartuzi2022 at 8.85 nM, chosen on completeness of printed conditions (the only source printing radioligand + concentration + human isoform + sodium + temperature + time + NSB together) and NOT on its value: it is the highest of the seven, so the choice cannot flatter the in-vitro/in-vivo agreement, and a test asserts both. RATIO: reported as the full set, 0.213 to 14.50, because one number would be a choice of denominator worth 68-fold. The range STRADDLES UNITY, so the in-vitro literature cannot even agree whether the in-vivo constant is larger or smaller than it is; no correction factor is recorded anywhere, and the occupancy path consumes the in-vivo EC50. EFFICACY, and this changed the record: haloperidol is an INVERSE AGONIST at human D2, not a neutral antagonist, by two independent readouts. Registered -0.95 (Hall & Strange 1997, whole-cell forskolin-stimulated cAMP, 0.95 +/- 0.03 of 1 uM (+)-butaclamol, n=3), with -0.83 ([35S]GTPgammaS, Roberts & Strange 2005, n=5) recorded alongside and the range stated rather than averaged. EFFICACY_SCALE writes down that the scale is asymmetric: 0 is neutral, positive is agonism referenced to the endogenous agonist, negative is inverse agonism referenced to (+)-butaclamol in that assay, and the two ends are not interconvertible, so -0.95 does not mean 95% as far below basal as dopamine is above it. Three limitations on the records themselves: both quantitative sources are from the SAME laboratory (Strange, Reading); Roberts's 83% is condition-specific because the authors deliberately maximised constitutive activity by omitting sodium and GDP; both use high heterologous expression. Burstein 2005 agrees on direction from an independent lab but is paywalled and prints no value, so it is recorded as a qualitative statement only and excluded from the efficacy set. SEARCHED AND EMPTY, recorded as results: no primary human TISSUE (post-mortem brain, caudate, striatum, pituitary) D2 haloperidol Ki was reachable, so every registered value is from a heterologous cell line and a test asserts that stays true; and no primary beta-arrestin measurement of haloperidol's efficacy at human D2 was retrievable across 30 screened open-access records (constitutive beta-arrestin recruitment at D2 is not routinely measurable, so this may be a real absence rather than a retrieval failure; only the non-retrieval is claimed). EXCLUDED with reasons: de Witte 2018 (its binding assay is never stated to use a human receptor), McCormick 2010 (rat brain), Kroeze 2003 (paywalled behind a false open-access signal, no number taken), Seeman & Van Tol 1995 (paywalled, cited for the effect only, no number used), PDSP (aggregator, not primary). Pirate mirrors excluded by instruction throughout, so paywalled means unavailable. Two stale tests in test_human_receptor_parameters.py were TIGHTENED rather than relaxed: the blanket 'no record is usable' assertion now asserts D2 is the only usable one and that the other five have neither an EC50 nor an efficacy nor a ligand, and the single-target rodent-fallback refusal now loops over all five remaining targets. tasks.notes: Delivered: predict_occupancy in src/neurocascade/human/dose_to_occupancy.py, the first end-to-end human chain in the repository. Dose, route, body weight and a time grid in; a striatal D2 occupancy-time curve out, carrying a ChainLayer per stage with its own status, citation and provenance, and a prediction-level provenance that is the weakest claim any layer makes. THREE DEPARTURES FROM THE OBVIOUS CONSTRUCTION, each of which is the finding rather than a shortcut around it. (1) TWO COMPARTMENTS, NOT THREE: the brief specified DosedThreeCompartmentPK, and P19.2 had already established that no human three-compartment haloperidol set exists (Holley 1983 prints only CL and Vss, Chang 1992 names the model and never prints its micro-constants, both paywalled and pirate mirrors excluded), so satisfying the brief would have meant inventing V3 and Q13. The chain dispatches on the compartment count the sourced record declares and raises for anything else, naming what is missing. (2) NO BRAIN-PARTITION STEP: the haloperidol Kp,uu record is absent/not-required, and the P19.4 EC50 was fitted against plasma measured in living people whose striatal occupancy was measured at the same time, so brain penetration, plasma protein binding and competition with endogenous dopamine are already inside it; multiplying by a Kp,uu as well would apply the same correction twice. The chain re-reads the record on every call and raises if a value has since appeared, rather than trusting that the design still holds. No brain_partition is attached, so the model reports its receptor compartment as total plasma. (3) BODY WEIGHT IS ACCEPTED AND THEN REFUSED: Pilla Reddy 2013 states an allometric exponent for clearance (0.75) and for nothing else, and because DosedTwoCompartmentPK takes per-kg parameters the naive conversion lets body weight cancel out of the kinetics entirely, silently asserting an exponent of 1 where the source printed 0.75. Any weight other than the source's 70 kg reference now raises unless the caller supplies a WeightScaling naming the volume and Q exponents and where they came from; clearance keeps the source's own exponent through CL_L_per_h_at_weight. GATING IS REAL, NOT BYPASSED: require_human_parameter('D2') succeeds for the first time (it could not before P19.4, when the record had no in-vivo EC50 and was not usable) and nothing in the chain works around it; the disposition parameters are passed apparent with apparent_parameters=True, so F stays folded in and is not borrowed from another study; _gate_illustrative applies the P19.1 opt-in to the whole layer set with the same literal ILLUSTRATIVE token every other gate in the package raises. No layer is illustrative today, so that gate currently refuses nothing and is tested directly rather than through a real prediction - stated in the docs rather than left to look like coverage. The transduction layer applies d2_effect at Emax 1 and baseline occupancy 0, neither of which has been fitted in a human, so abs(effect) equals occupancy exactly; a test asserts that identity so the claim 'a re-expression of occupancy, not a behavioural claim' is checkable rather than a promise in a docstring. PREDICTIONS, single oral dose in a 70 kg subject, not yet compared to anything: 5 mg peaks at 5.21 nM total plasma (1.96 ng/mL) at 195 min and 0.734 striatal occupancy, falling to 0.483 at 24 h; peak occupancy 0.356 at 1 mg, 0.624 at 3 mg, 0.847 at 10 mg, 0.917 at 20 mg, so forty times the dose is four times the occupancy. Terminal half-life 31.1 h, tmax 195 min. Whether those numbers are right is P19.6's question and is not assumed here; the EC50 behind them was fitted on depot intramuscular steady-state observations applied to an oral chain, a mismatch carried forward from P19.4 and printed in the occupancy layer's own text. REFUSALS, each a test and not a comment: a PK record missing any of V1_L, V2_L, Q12_L_per_h, CL_L_per_h or ka_per_min (the acceptance criterion's removed required parameter); a receptor record with the in-vivo EC50 removed, which is what a Ki-only record looks like; a free-basis EC50 against a total-plasma PK layer; route IV, because P19.2 recorded that search as empty, and any route with no record at all; an off-reference body weight with no stated scaling rule; a Kp,uu record that has acquired a value; a PK record for another drug or species and a receptor record for another ligand; a reporting grid that is not strictly increasing, starts before the dose, or has fewer than two points; and reading an occupancy at a time outside the computed window. The reporting grid is a display choice, not a model parameter: a test asserts a tenfold finer grid gives the same occupancy at the same times. 26 new tests in tests/test_human_dose_to_occupancy.py; full gate 2146 passed, 4 skipped, 15 deselected, exit 0. Docs: docs/p19-5-dose-to-occupancy-chain.md plus a new architecture.md section.

tasks.title: Partial agonism breaks the occupancy-limited transducer

tasks.brief: Train a transparent model mapping a drug's panel occupancy/activation profile (at clinical dose) to the binary clinical-effect vector, on the train split. Keep it interpretable (per-effect regularised logistic or similar) so each effect's receptor drivers are inspectable. No held-out drug enters the fit. This is the product's flagship layer (decided 2026-10-12 audit): PK is a commodity, the interpretable occupancy-to-CNS-liability map is the differentiator. Labels must be placebo-subtracted: an effect is positive when drug incidence exceeds placebo incidence by the stated margin in the label/trial table; where no placebo arm is published, record that and use the absolute rule as a flagged fallback, never silently. Exposure input (re-pointed 2026-10-13 so the flagship is not blocked behind P29.3/P29.4/P29.5): compute clinical-dose occupancy from OBSERVED human exposure, i.e. the P28.4 clinical dose with observed human CL/F (or a published steady-state Cmax/Cavg), unbound fraction where recorded, the human Ki panel and the P29.1 Kp,uu where available.
